title: Protocol for evaluating the role of a gene in protecting mouse retinal ganglion cells
protocol: Weigh each adult mouse and inject the appropriate amount of anesthetic solution (ketamine-100 mg/kg and xylazine-10 mg/kg) intraperitoneally.
Keep the animal in a container until there is no response to a toe pinch.
Align the eyeball in the viewing field center of the stereomicroscope.
Clip the lower eyelid with a bulldog clamp.
Secure the eyeball to a steady position.
Leave a small portion of the virus solution in the micropipette to avoid air or oil entering the vitreous.
Pre-warm the heating pad and underpads when starting the experiment.
Load a set volume of AAV solution into the micropipette.
Draw a line on the micropipette to mark the injection volume.
Adjust the angle and inserting depth of the micropipette to avoid touching the lens or retina.
Insert the micropipette just behind the ora serrata.
Hold the micropipette steady and slowly push the plunger with the other hand to inject the virus solution into the vitreous.
Control the speed of injection (10–15 s/μL).
If the virus solution contains fast green, observe the dye spreading inside the vitreous.
Hold the micropipette in position for a few more seconds and gently pull it out of the eyeball.
Release the bulldog clamp after intravitreal injection.
Let the eyeball stand for 30 s.
Gently move the eyelids with forceps to help the eyeball back into orbit.
Apply antibiotic ointment onto the eye to prevent infection and dryness.
Put the mouse on underpads warmed by a heating pad (37 degrees Celsius) in a container.
Monitor the condition of the mouse periodically until it wakes up, then return it to the cage.
Wait two weeks after intravitreal AAV injection before proceeding.
Secure the mouse head position using the head holder.
Turn the head holder to make the right eye face upward for a right-handed operator or the left eye face upward for a left-handed operator.
Align the eyeball in the viewing field center of the surgical microscope.
Use a pair of forceps to expose the eyeball from the ventral/temporal side.
Open the connective tissues covering the optic nerve using another pair of forceps.
Adjust microscope focal plane to focus on the optic nerve.
Crush the optic nerve for 5 s at approximately 1 mm behind the globe.
Clean all surgical instruments with 75% ethanol before each use.
Perform rapid transcardial perfusion with 4% PFA according to general procedures.
Fix the eyeball in 4% PFA post-perfusion.
Place the plate on a shaker during fixation.
Enucleate the eyeball using a pair of forceps right after perfusion.
Clean up the eyeball in PBS and make a small opening on the cornea.
Transfer the eyeball into 2 mL 4% PFA in a well of 24-well plate.
Put the plate on a shaker for 1–2 h at room temperature.
Dissect the retina out of the eyeball after fixation.
Gently and thoroughly clean the inner surface of the retina with forceps or a synthetic sable paint brush.
Cut the retinal cup into a cross shape.
Transfer the retina into a 1.5 mL tube.
Incubate in 1.2 mL blocking buffer for 1 h.
Incubate the retina in 200 μL primary antibody (Tuj1) solution (1:250) at room temperature overnight (16–20 h).
Wash the retina in 1.2 mL PBS 3 times for 15 min each.
Incubate the retina in 200 μL secondary antibody solution (1:500) at room temperature for 2 h.
Wash the retina in 1.2 mL PBS 3 times for 15 min each.
Transfer the retina onto a slide with the RGC side facing up.
Remove PBS solution from the retina.
Apply Fluoromount-G mounting medium to the slide.
Mount the retina under a cover glass horizontally.
Take confocal images of retinal whole-mounts using a Zeiss LSM 800 microscope.
Use a 20× objective lens to image a 320 × 320 μm square area.
Locate the center of the sampling square at approximately 500 μm from the edge of the retinal flat-mounts leading to the optic disc.
Sample 3 squares in each petal of the retinal whole-mount.
Sample a total of 12 squares for one retinal whole-mount.
Use Tuj1 immunostaining to label both RGC somas and axons.
Take Z-stack confocal images focusing on RGC somas for each square.
Generate a composite image using maximum intensity Z-projection for RGC counting.
Open the image in ImageJ and click “Plugins>Analyze>Cell Counter” to open the control panel.
Click “Initialize” in the “Actions” region to prepare the image for counting.
Choose one “Type number” in the “Counter” region.
Click each RGC soma once to count RGCs.
A dot will mark the cell after a click.
Quantify the number of RGCs in an image and record it.
Average RGC numbers from all 12 squares in a retina.
Collect multiple retinas for each experimental group.
Calculate "mean" and "standard deviation (s.d.)" for comparison among groups.
Make graphs using GraphPad or other statistical software.
Calculate percentages of RGCs relative to those in the uninjured retina.
Evaluate RGC survival after experimental manipulations/treatments using absolute numbers and percentages.
